answer_text:
Let

\[
H_n=1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1n
\]

be the \(n\)-th harmonic number. We need

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n}{(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}\ln n}.
\]

First, estimate \(H_n\). Since \(1/x\) is decreasing,

\[
\int_1^{n+1}\frac{dx}{x}\le H_n\le 1+\int_1^n\frac{dx}{x}.
\]

Thus

\[
\ln(n+1)\le H_n\le 1+\ln n.
\]

Dividing by \(\ln n\),

\[
\frac{\ln(n+1)}{\ln n}\le \frac{H_n}{\ln n}\le 1+\frac1{\ln n}.
\]

Both bounds tend to \(1\), so

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n}{\ln n}=1.
\]

Now evaluate the other factor:

\[
(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}
=
\left(\pi^n\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)\right)^{1/n}
=
\pi\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)^{1/n}.
\]

Since \(e/\pi<1\),

\[
\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\to 0,
\]

and therefore

\[
\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)^{1/n}\to 1.
\]

Hence

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}=\pi.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{H_n}{(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}\ln n}
=
\frac{\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n}{\ln n}}
{\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}}
=
\frac{1}{\pi}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{\pi}}
\]

27B·v4.method: Asymptotic of harmonic sum (H_n ~ ln n) and n-th root of exponential sum (→ π), then quotient of limits gives 1/π.
